statement: Encrypted archives end in exactly 192 bytes: existing footer magic, version 2, length 192, flags 0, total container length, envelope and segments offsets/lengths, terminal segment and ArchiveFinal offsets, preamble, segments-payload and PublicCryptoContext SHA-256 digests, 24 zero bytes.

FooterCoreV1 is a T1 transcript of footer version, total length, envelope/segments offsets and lengths, terminal segment and ArchiveFinal offsets, preamble digest and public crypto context digest; ArchiveFinalV1 stores its SHA-256, avoiding circular dependency on ciphertext.

The footer's unkeyed segments digest is excluded from FooterCore and checked only as an exact corruption checksum; AEAD, SegmentEnd and ArchiveFinal provide security, and any footer locator or length used for acceptance must match the authenticated FooterCore.

PublicCryptoContextV1 is a derived, never separately serialized T1 transcript of namespace, format major/minor, crypto version, suite ID, archive ID, layout, role, required features, padding mode and boundary mode; preamble and envelope sources must agree.

CryptoEnvelopeV1 fields are crypto version 1, payload suite 1, 32-byte archive ID, 32-byte commitment, protection policy, padding mode, boundary mode, exact RecipientStanzaSequenceV1 bytes and a 32-byte envelope MAC.
RecipientStanzaSequenceV1 is count:u64be followed by length:u64be plus exact stanza record, in canonical order; it is a field-local public grammar without magic, not an EBCS private container.
Stanza limits of 1,024 stanzas, 64 KiB per stanza and 16 MiB total envelope are enforced before allocation, and encrypted archives require a nonempty stanza sequence.
The 1,024-stanza, 64 KiB-per-stanza and 16 MiB envelope limits are numeric parameters chosen without cited measurement.

statement: EnvelopeCoreV1 is a T1 transcript of canonical PublicCryptoContextV1, commitment, protection policy and exact stanza sequence bytes; the envelope MAC construction is defined in crypto-suite-v1.md.

RecipientStanzaV1 fields are version 1, stanza type, protection class, random 16-byte stanza ID, 16-byte recipient hint, bounded method parameters, method encapsulation (1120 bytes X-Wing, empty password), random 12-byte wrap nonce and 48-byte wrapped AFK.

The recipient hint must be exactly 16 zero bytes in v1, so no recipient key hints exist and identities are matched by trial against every stanza; populated hints are implicitly reserved for later versions.

statement: For X-Wing stanzas field 6 is the exact ASCII method string; for password stanzas field 6 is the 36-byte A2ID structure defined in the suite document.
Stanzas are sorted ascending by (SHA-256 of T1 recipient-stanza-sort/v1 over exact stanza bytes, exact stanza bytes); exact duplicate stanza bytes are forbidden.
Writers must deduplicate identical input recipient public keys before encapsulation using a private key fingerprint; readers cannot and need not detect semantically duplicate randomized stanzas.
Unknown stanza types keep the canonical outer fields and limits; they may be skipped during matching but remain in the sorted sequence and under the MAC.

recipient_set_digest is SHA-256 of T1 recipient-set/v1 over the exact sorted sequence; it is input-order independent, includes unknown stanzas, changes with any stanza field, and is used in ArchiveFinal and the addressing signature binding.

statement: AEAD DATA plaintext is private_length:u64be, the exact PrivateFragmentV1 record, then random padding; private_length covers only the record, and padding length is derived from plaintext length with no second padding-size field.

PrivateFragmentV1 carries 32-byte encrypted object ID, complete object length, zero-based fragment index, nonzero fragment count, fragment byte offset and exact fragment bytes; object_id is SHA-256 of T1 encrypted-object/v1 over complete object bytes.

Fragments of one object are contiguous, ordered, gap-free, non-overlapping and collectively exact, reassembling one PrivateObjectV1; no fragment is parsed as an inner object before complete authenticated reassembly.

statement: Every complete encrypted object has a 12-byte header (magic EBPO, version 1, private_object_kind u16be, flags 0) followed by payload extending to the exact complete-object length from the fragment declaration.

PrivateObjectV1 has no payload-length field because the fragment declaration solely owns object extent; it is a standalone crypto framing grammar, not an ECF record, and its kind is physical parser dispatch rather than a semantic type.

CANONICAL_RECORD payload is exactly one ECF record including its 16-byte header; CHUNK_FRAME payload is exactly one versioned EBCH frame; SEQUENCE_CONTAINER payload is exactly one EBCS container; no trailing bytes.

Dispatch and payload grammar must agree; nested EBPO, unknown object kinds, wrong inner magic/version, trailing bytes and complete objects over 2^30 bytes are rejected before semantic use, eliminating format-guessing heuristics.

statement: The empty sequence for kind K is exactly magic EBCS, version 0001, K, zero flags and zero item count, and is canonical only when the kind-specific cardinality permits emptiness.

Unknown container kinds fail closed as EB_CRYPTO_SUITE_UNSUPPORTED and malformed known containers as EB_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID; parsers dispatch on EBPO kind, then container_kind, then enforce item types and order, never inferring a collection from contents.
MANIFEST (kind 1) holds Entry records (3) ordered by canonical LogicalPath, then ContentObject records (4) ordered by logical digest; it may be empty, and duplicate paths or digests are forbidden.
TRANSFORM_PLANS (kind 2) holds TransformPlan records (2) by plan ID ascending; it must be nonempty and duplicate IDs are forbidden.
DICTIONARIES (kind 3) holds Dictionary records (11) by dictionary digest ascending; empty allowed, duplicate digests forbidden.
CHUNK_GROUPS (kind 4) holds ChunkGroup records (12) by group ID ascending; empty allowed, duplicate IDs forbidden.
RECONSTRUCTION_DATA_AND_AUDIT (kind 5) holds ReconstructionData (14) by reconstruction digest, then ReconstructionFallback (16) by Chunk digest; empty allowed, duplicate targets/digests forbidden.

RECONSTRUCTION_REGIONS_AND_AUDIT (kind 6) holds ReconstructionRegion (18) by region ID, then ReconstructionAudit v2 (19) by (target kind, target digest, transform ID) byte tuple; empty allowed, duplicates forbidden.

After commitment and envelope-MAC verification the Descriptor must be the first authenticated private object, and its declaration is checked against caller policy before dependent private objects are accepted.

Readers independently aggregate decoder requirements from authenticated plans, dictionaries and groups and derive actuals from the complete EAM; requirements must match the declaration and actuals must stay within every declared upper bound.

statement: END plaintext uses the same private_length, record and random padding framing and contains segment ordinal, segment class, DATA record count, aggregate unpadded DATA private bytes, aggregate DATA ciphertext bytes, and DATA transcript digest.

The DATA transcript digest is SHA-256 of T1 segment-data/v1 over the exact segment header and the length-prefixed protected headers and ciphertexts in counter order; the END record is excluded from its own digest.
A completed segment digest used by ArchiveFinal is SHA-256 of T1 segment-digest/v1 over exact segment header, DATA header/ciphertext sequence, END header and END ciphertext.
END record padding always uses CONTROL bucket/capacity rules, even inside a PAYLOAD segment.
The last segment is CONTROL and contains exactly one DATA object, the ArchiveFinalV1 record, followed by its END record and nothing else.

ArchiveFinalV1 records total segment count, actual entry count, total logical bytes, unique Chunk count, LAI, PCR, AUX, recipient-set digest, prior-segment sequence digest, FooterCore digest, and object IDs of the authoritative Descriptor and manifest root.
The prior-segment sequence digest is SHA-256 of T1 segment-sequence/v1 over the nonterminal segment count and each 32-byte completed segment digest in ordinal order.

Descriptor v2 carries final resource/decode requirements and identities; ArchiveFinal repeats identities and totals only as a terminal physical authentication assertion; the authenticated Descriptor/EAM stays semantic authority, equality is mandatory, and mismatch is corruption.
Readers verify exact footer/EOF, public section digests, every relevant segment and END, ArchiveFinal, Descriptor/EAM constraints and identities, and PCI over the exact bytes.
A missing footer or incomplete promised extent is TRUNCATED; a present complete extent with a failed digest, tag or binding is CORRUPT or INTEGRITY_MISMATCH.
research_needed: The crypto reason-code table maps failures to INTEGRITY_MISMATCH/NONCONFORMING but never CORRUPT; confirm when CORRUPT applies.

statement: SignatureRecordV1 fields: version 1, algorithm 1, binding mask (bit 0 required, no unknown bits), raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, ContentBindingV1, PhysicalBindingV1 iff bit 1, AddressingBindingV1 iff bit 2, 64-byte signature, optional DER RFC 3161 token up to 64 KiB.
The signer identifier is derived from the public key field and is not serialized.
ContentBindingV1 binds LAI, AUX, the identity/v1 label, the ecf/bootstrap-v1 namespace and format major/minor, excluding PCR and PCI, so content signatures can survive physical repacking.

Because ContentBindingV1 includes format_major/minor, re-encoding identical content under a later format version (e.g. leaving 0.1) would make content signatures stale even when LAI/AUX are unchanged.
research_needed: Evaluate signature longevity across format version bumps and migrations.
decision_needed: Should the content binding include container format version, or only identity-profile version?

statement: PhysicalBindingV1 binds only the PCR.
AddressingBindingV1 binds payload suite ID, recipient-set digest, commitment and archive ID.

Signed bytes are a T1 signature/v1 transcript of version, algorithm, mask, signer key, ContentBinding, physical-present flag, PhysicalBinding or empty, addressing-present flag, and AddressingBinding or empty.
Ed25519 signs the transcript bytes directly in pure mode, not a SHA-256 prehash.
For timestamps, the RFC 3161 messageImprint is SHA-256 (id-sha256) of the canonical type-26 record through tag 8; the token itself is tag 9 and excluded from that hash.
Timestamp tokens are validated against imprint, signature, chain and time policy, but trust anchors, acceptable TSAs and default time policy are not defined in this document.
research_needed: Locate or define TSA trust anchor configuration and default policy; check platform trust-store availability.
decision_needed: What are the default RFC 3161 trust anchors and time-validation policy?

statement: Embedded signature records are encrypted CONTROL objects; a detached .ebsig file is exactly one canonical type-26 record with no container wrapper.

statement: A detached signature does not alter the archive's required-feature bitmap.
A future feature may add a recipient type but cannot change the interpretation of any numeric value assigned in this specification.
Crypto diagnostics use existing top-level classes; public CLI output is 'reason-code: concise detail' and never Rust debug formatting.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_SUITE_UNSUPPORTED has class UNSUPPORTED and denotes unknown crypto or suite version, or unknown critical algorithm.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED has class UNSUPPORTED and denotes encrypted STREAM or unseekable output requested in v1.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_NO_MATCHING_RECIPIENT has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes supplied identities unlock no supported stanza, or the attempt budget is exhausted.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_STANZA_INVALID has class NONCONFORMING and denotes invalid stanza framing, sizes, reserved fields, type/class or policy.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_POLICY_INVALID has class NONCONFORMING and denotes hybrid/password mixing, stanza cardinality or protection policy mismatch.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_ENVELOPE_AUTH_FAILED has class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and denotes authenticated wrap/envelope check failure with wrong-secret detail suppressed.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_KEY_COMMITMENT_FAILED has class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and denotes authenticated candidate AFK not matching stored commitment, using the same public unlock wording.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_PASSWORD_KDF_POLICY_REFUSED has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes valid encoded Argon2id cost exceeding caller policy.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_AEAD_AUTH_FAILED has class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and denotes protected-record tag failure, releasing no plaintext.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_SEGMENT_STRUCTURE_INVALID has class NONCONFORMING and denotes violated ordinal, counter, salt reuse, count, END, terminal or ordering rules.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_PADDING_INVALID has class NONCONFORMING and denotes invalid padding mode, bucket, private length or padding framing.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_PRIVATE_OBJECT_INVALID has class NONCONFORMING and denotes invalid EBPO/EBCS magic, version, flags, kind agreement, extent, item type/order/cardinality or inner canonical bytes.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_BOUNDARY_MODE_UNSUPPORTED has class UNSUPPORTED and denotes an authenticated required boundary mode that is not implemented.
Reason code EB_CRYPTO_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes crypto framing, identity attempts or decrypted declared requirements exceeding caller policy.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_ABSENT has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes caller policy requiring a signature when none exists.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_UNSUPPORTED has class UNSUPPORTED and denotes unknown signature version or algorithm.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_INVALID has class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and denotes signature bytes or key encoding failing strict verification.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_CONTENT has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes a valid signature whose content binding differs when the caller requires it current.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_PHYSICAL has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes a valid signature whose physical binding differs when the caller requires it current.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_ADDRESSING has class POLICY_REFUSED and denotes a valid signature whose addressing binding differs when the caller requires it current.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID has class INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and denotes a supported timestamp token failing imprint, signature, chain or time policy.
Reason code EB_SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP_UNSUPPORTED has class UNSUPPORTED and denotes a token using a non-v1 CMS, imprint or signature algorithm.

The existence of EB_CRYPTO_BOUNDARY_MODE_UNSUPPORTED implies a conforming reader may omit a frozen boundary mode (e.g. PHTE_AES128), but the document does not say which boundary modes are mandatory for readers.
